import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Feit-Thompson conjecture on primes

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feit%E2%80%93Thompson_conjecture)
-/

namespace FeitThompsonPrimeConjecture

/--
There are no distinct primes $p$ and $q$ such that $\frac{q^p - 1}{q - 1}$ divides $\frac{p^q - 1}{p - 1}$
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem feit_thompson_primes (p q : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (hq : q.Prime) (h : p < q) :
    ¬ (q ^ p - 1) / (q - 1) ∣ (p ^ q - 1) / (p - 1) := by
  sorry

end FeitThompsonPrimeConjecture

reformulations.difference: Wikipedia excludes (p^q − 1)/(p − 1) dividing (q^p − 1)/(q − 1) for all distinct primes. Lean interchanges the labels and restricts its hypothesis to p < q rather than p ≠ q.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Write R(b,n) = (b^n − 1)/(b − 1). For all natural numbers 2 ≤ a < b, we proved 0 < R(b,a) < R(a,b); consequently R(a,b) cannot divide R(b,a). Thus the omitted ordering is automatically impossible by size. Splitting Wikipedia's distinct primes into the two orderings, one case follows from this inequality and the other is precisely the Lean statement with labels exchanged. Conversely, Wikipedia's statement immediately implies Lean's by exchanging labels and restricting the ordering. The full equivalence was proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean as Review.wikipedia_iff_file, without invoking the conjecture; its axiom dependencies contain no sorryAx.

review.notes: Checked the file's sole declaration. Prime hypotheses exclude 0 and 1, ensure positive denominators, and prevent truncated subtraction from changing the expressions. Lean proofs establish that both natural-number quotients are exact geometric sums and equal the corresponding rational expressions. Boundary instances and all 300 increasing prime pairs below 100 passed computational checks. The Stephens pair (17,3313) has gcd 112643 but still satisfies nondivisibility, consistent with Wikipedia's distinction between this conjecture and the disproved stronger coprimality conjecture. The research-open category agrees with the current cited source. All experiments are under /workspace/review/; the reviewed file matches the specified commit.
